samples.question: The pawn starts in the colored-ringed room. Rooms are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right by black-dot count. Each gate is OPEN when its two colored bars lie along the corridor and CLOSED when they cross it. Read the six cards from left to right. A colored-background card flips the gate named by its black-dot count. A white arrow card tries to move the pawn one room in its direction; it moves only when the gate between the rooms is OPEN, and otherwise stays. The pawn also stays if an arrow points beyond the corridor. Which room contains the pawn at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.
